The current-vintage paths, sizes and modification times were sealed in launch.json; the six exact local tables are the sources declared in work/submission.json. No observation-level data were copied into the report.
changes: Extended the annual pooled sample on its original FYEAR clock from 1951–2001 through FYEAR 2006, with FYEAR 1950 retained as lag support.

Moved the accepted CRSP DSI/DSF and Compustat security daily/monthly source filters from 31 December 2003 to 31 December 2008, retaining the 1 January 1948 lower bound so current DATADATE windows and prior-price lookups remain covered.

Added aggregate source date coverage summaries to the SAS build and counted the original and added ranges on the actual Stata e(sample); retained the handoff FYEAR column and emitted the required EXT_SAMPLE line.

Saved a fresh aggregate coefficient and sample-count table at work/artifacts/annual_pooled_eq1.csv. The pooled OLS terms, price/return construction, date-effective link and currency screens, annual trimming, and accepted best-effort choices were retained.
limitations: Inherited specification ambiguity remains: the paper gives alternative annual Return windows without identifying which produced the pooled fit and does not identify the estimator or inference procedure. The accepted construction continues to use fiscal-year returns compounded over actual adjacent DATADATE endpoints and pooled OLS with conventional standard errors.

The original study used Compustat 2001 products and its cited CRSP data file. The replay uses the named current merged Compustat and CRSP vintages; it is not a vintage-identical reconstruction of the historical source population. The fit remains the accepted best-effort implementation.
This assignment covers only the pooled annual Equation 1 coefficient. The paper’s quarterly estimates, simulations, and subsequent robustness or event analyses are outside this assigned scope.

The paper reports β2 = 0.302; the accepted predecessor reconstruction reported 0.2837306. The current pooled replay reports 0.300660. These comparisons do not resolve the paper’s return-window ambiguity or vintage differences.
